compensating.why: hop 1 collapses runs of whitespace in the string before it is parsed
hop 3 trims the string before it is parsed
hop 4 uses the parser's own throwing parse of a String

expected_signature: Expected FDF failure, but got null for [M E,3  Tue]
ownership_reason: Only the gold calls the parser and decides whether its result is a date; hops 2-4 pass the parser, the string, the message lead and the expected form along unchanged and hop 1 only composes the lead (the note on the supported date range of the imperial locale). The gold's javadoc promises to parse the beginning of a string to produce a date as DateParser#parse(String) does and to return the parsed date; for "3  Tue" against "M E" it returns null instead of the ParseException that DateParser#parse(String) documents ('@throws ParseException if the beginning of the specified string cannot be parsed'). The null result of the parser is its documented error signal (DateParser#parse(String, ParsePosition): 'In case of error, returns null'; FastDateParser.parse(String, ParsePosition) returns null when the pattern does not match), and DateUtils.parseDateWithLeniency, the sibling in the gold's own class, treats exactly that null as no match and throws ParseException (DateUtilsTest testParseDate, testParseDateWithLeniency and testLANG799_EN_FAIL pass). No one-line change of the values above the gold makes the non-matching string throw: collapsing its whitespace makes it match as a date where a failure is required, trimming changes nothing, and the parser's own throwing parse(String) is the facade itself.
